learning_outcomes.text: Analyze the capacity to fulfill the structural function of resistant elements subjected to different loads.
Know the applicable regulations to ensure the integrity of critical structures.
With this knowledge, the student will be able to approach damage-tolerant designs applicable in various industry sectors, such as aerospace, transportation, and energy.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
Adequate knowledge of their engineering branch, including some cutting-edge knowledge in their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.
Awareness of all implications of engineering practice.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of engineering practice.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to meet the required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply current legislation as well as mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards in the field of mechanical engineering.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.

syllabus_topics: Fracture criteria in elastic and linear materials
Elementary notions of fracture under dynamic conditions
Subcritical crack propagation due to fatigue and other effects
Fatigue life calculation of mechanical components
Numerical methods in fatigue and fracture
assessment_rules: To pass the course, attendance and completion of the laboratory practices scheduled weekly are mandatory. The weighting of the practical grade in the continuous assessment corresponds to 60% of the continuous assessment grade.
bibliography: Anderson, T.L.. Fracture mechanics: Fundamentals and applications. CRC Press. 1995
Anglada, M.J.. Fractura de materiales. UPC. 2002
Broek, David. Elementary engineering fracture mechanics. Kluwer Academic. 1991
Kanninen, Melvin F.. Advanced fracture mechanics. Oxford University Press. 1985
